hints: Resolve forces parallel to the hill (down the slope) separately for the trailer ($750\text{ kg}$) and the van ($4500\text{ kg}$).
For the trailer moving downhill, the forces acting down the slope are its component of weight $mg \sin \theta$ and the tow-bar tension $T = 450\text{ N}$, opposed by resistance $300\text{ N}$.
Apply $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ to the trailer to solve for $a$, then apply $F_{\text{net}} = Ma$ to the van (or whole system) to find the driving force $D$.
walkthrough:
Set up the equation of motion down the slope for the trailer. The forces acting down the slope are the component of the trailer's weight $m_t g \sin \theta$ and the forward pull of the tow-bar tension $T = 450\text{ N}$. Opposing the motion up the slope is the resistance force $R_t = 300\text{ N}$:
$$m_t g \sin \theta + T - R_t = m_t a$$

Divide both sides by $750$ to determine the acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{525}{750} = \frac{7}{10} = 0.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Now set up the equation of motion down the slope for the van ($M_v = 4500\text{ kg}$). The forward forces down the incline are the driving force $D$ and the component of the van's weight $M_v g \sin \theta$. The opposing forces up the incline are the backward tension of the tow-bar $T = 450\text{ N}$ and the resistance $R_v = 2500\text{ N}$:
$$D + M_v g \sin \theta - T - R_v = M_v a$$

Add $700$ to both sides to find the driving force $D$:
$$D = 3150 + 700 = 3850\text{ N}$$

hints: For the uphill motion with $\sin \alpha = 0.09$, both the weight components and resistances act down the slope opposing the motion.
Form Newton's second law equations for the trailer ($T - mg \sin \alpha - R_t = ma$) and for the van ($D - T - Mg \sin \alpha - R_v = Ma$), with driving force $D = 9100\text{ N}$.
Add the two equations to eliminate $T$ and solve for $a$, then substitute $a$ back to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Set up the equations of motion for the system ascending the hill inclined at $\sin \alpha = 0.09$. Both vehicles experience downward weight components along the slope:
For the trailer: $m_t g \sin \alpha = 750(10)(0.09) = 675\text{ N}$.
For the van: $M_v g \sin \alpha = 4500(10)(0.09) = 4050\text{ N}$.

For the trailer ($m_t = 750\text{ kg}$), the tow-bar pulls it up the hill with tension $T$, opposed by weight component and resistance $R_t = 300\text{ N}$:
$$T - m_t g \sin \alpha - R_t = m_t a$$
$$T - 675 - 300 = 750a$$
$$T - 975 = 750a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

For the van ($M_v = 4500\text{ kg}$), the forward driving force is $D = 9100\text{ N}$, opposed by tension $T$ pulling backwards, weight component, and resistance $R_v = 2500\text{ N}$:
$$D - T - M_v g \sin \alpha - R_v = M_v a$$
$$9100 - T - 4050 - 2500 = 4500a$$
$$2550 - T = 4500a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to eliminate $T$:
$$(T - 975) + (2550 - T) = 750a + 4500a$$
$$1575 = 5250a$$

Divide both sides by $5250$:
$$a = \frac{1575}{5250} = \frac{3}{10} = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Substitute $a = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ into Equation 1 to find the tension $T$:
$$T - 975 = 750(0.3)$$
$$T - 975 = 225$$
$$T = 975 + 225 = 1200\text{ N}$$
The acceleration of the van is $0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the tow-bar is $1200\text{ N}$.

hints: Identify the kinematic parameters for the ascent: initial speed $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, distance $s = 375\text{ m}$, and acceleration $a = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Apply the constant acceleration relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ and solve for $v$.
walkthrough: Identify the known values for the uphill motion: initial velocity at the bottom of the hill $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, constant acceleration $a = 0.3\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and distance travelled $s = 375\text{ m}$.

Select the constant acceleration formula connecting $u$, $v$, $a$, and $s$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$

Take the positive square root to find the speed:
$$v = \sqrt{625} = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
